selection_rationale: autocand-2026-01 best matches the programme’s primary gap (G1) by providing a preregistered, paired, reproducible comparison of LLM-only vs LLM+RAG vs LLM+RAG+Verifier on realistic change tasks; it has high falsifiability, strong venue relevance, and feasible compute needs while enabling clear primary outcomes (actionable misconfiguration rate reductions) supported by the cited feasibility/novelty records.
unresolved_uncertainties: Simulator/digital‑twin fidelity vs production networks (construct validity).
Degree to which retriever/corpus quality vs RAG design drive observed benefits (confounding).
Formal verifier false negatives or modeling mismatches that bias efficacy estimates.
LLM nondeterminism, API limits, and their impact on variance and required model calls.
How semantic policy gaps (intent underspecification) vs generator errors contribute to residual failures.
Sensitivity of results to retriever/embedding/threshold hyperparameters and vendor‑CLI heterogeneity.
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Specify exact public topology sources and CLI emulation toolchain (images, versions) and publish hashes.
Prespecify retriever architecture, embedding model, index parameters, and retrieval seeds (and include sensitivity analysis ranges).
Select and justify a concrete verifier implementation (e.g., Batfish/NetKAT variant); document modeling assumptions and known limitations.
Provide explicit labeling/adjudication rules for actionable misconfiguration, and prespecify resolution procedure for simulator/verifier disagreements.
Prespecify exact LLM model identifiers, temperature/decoding settings, retry policy, random seeds, and maximum model-call budget for reproducibility.
